failures.name: Concurrent-Write Data Loss (DL-019)
failures.severity: High — 432 items across Pack C (243) and Pack D (189) silently overwritten
failures.what_happened: Two concurrent sessions operated on the same pack files without write-lock coordination. The DL-013/certification-wave session wrote to Pack C and Pack D from a disk snapshot that predated the DL-008 remediation session, causing 432 cleared ExplanationWrong[CorrectChoice] fields to be restored to their pre-fix state.
failures.root_cause: No file-lock or session-coordination mechanism existed. Multiple sessions ran in parallel on the same files. Write-then-scan-wrong methodology: scans verified fixes immediately post-remediation but no post-overwrite re-verification occurred.
failures.detection: Cross-session DL-008 re-verification scan found violations restored. A count that regressed 0→432 indicated concurrent-write overwrite.
failures.lesson: Every write session must be preceded by a backup and followed by independent post-write re-verification. No two write sessions may operate on the same pack file concurrently.
failures.prevention: BACKUP_PROTOCOL.md mandated (AGENTS.md §3). Session isolation enforced — 700-series explicitly tracked which packs each session modified. 800-series governance correction lane separately documented. Still no formal .lock file protocol (deferred).

failures.name: Brace-Matcher Undercount (DL-020)
failures.severity: High — caused false negatives on DL-008 detection (336 items missed), phantom DL-026 counts on clean files (75/63/47 discrepancy), and false TIER 1 classification of P1-AD-075 as 'missing content block'
failures.what_happened: The ExplanationValidator.extractQuestions() method used a naive bracket counter (depth increment/decrement on {/}) without tracking whether the parser was inside a JSON string value. Brackets inside string values caused the counter to misidentify array boundaries, producing truncated/corrupted question objects and silent false negatives.
failures.root_cause: No string-awareness in the parser (no inString/stringChar/escape state machine). The do...while loop tracked only { and } with no awareness of JSON string literals. Nested braces inside Choices.{A,B,C,D} objects were misinterpreted as object boundaries.
failures.detection: 197-vs-336 counting discrepancy on DL-008 scan — the validator's brace-matcher dropped corrupted objects. 75/63/47 discrepancy on Pack D Section D — three different runs of the same broken tool produced three different counts on a file that was already clean.
failures.lesson: Any parser operating on JSON source files must be string-aware. Compare parser-reported item counts against grep -c '"QuestionID"' as a standing sanity check. Never accept totals-only reports without QID lists.
failures.prevention: String-aware parser applied to extractQuestions() and extractCases(). DL-029 8 Permanent Prevention Rules mandate Function-constructor parse ONLY for all defect scans, string-aware brace-matchers for all parsers, and two independent scans must converge on identical count before any remediation.
evidence_refs: REVISION_HISTORY.md lines 8027–8091 (75/63/47 phantom count root cause)
REVISION_HISTORY.md lines 8929–8953 (AD-075 false TIER 1 root cause)

failures.name: Regex Block-Scan DL-008 False Positives (DL-029)
failures.severity: Critical — caused prior sessions to report 885+ Certified DL-008 where actual count was near-zero. S800's three P0 blockers (67 Certified DL-008, FD-045 missing, FD-075 missing) were all DL-029 artifacts. Nearly launched S801 as a massive false-alarm DL-008 remediation that would have modified hundreds of clean items.
failures.what_happened: CorrectChoice appears BEFORE QuestionID in all 5 pack file JSON objects (universal, not Pack-B-only). Regex block-window scanners that search forward from QuestionID systematically capture the NEXT item's CorrectChoice, producing a ~75% false-positive rate. Session 700 reported 341 Pack D DL-008; actual was ~20. Session 800 reported 67 Certified DL-008; actual was 0. SESSION_STATUS_2026-07-24 reported 10; actual was 20.
failures.root_cause: Scan methodology assumed CorrectChoice follows QuestionID (as in most JSON conventions). All 5 packs use CC-before-QID ordering. Forward-scan never verified CC position in source file before running. Totals-only reports accepted without QID-list verification per AGENTS.md §5.
failures.detection: S802 governance correction compared Function-constructor parse results (within-object CC extraction) against prior forward-scan reports. All 67 Certified DL-008 claims refuted. FD-045 and FD-075 structurally verified as complete.
failures.lesson: Never forward-scan for CorrectChoice from QuestionID. Verify CC position in source file before any scan. Function-constructor parse ONLY for all defect scans (within-object CC extraction). Two independent methods must converge. Reject totals-only reports without QID lists.
failures.prevention: DL-029 8 Permanent Prevention Rules codified: (1) Function-constructor parse ONLY, (2) never forward-scan CC from QID, (3) verify CC position first, (4) self-verify every scan against two methods, (5) all scan scripts must be CC-position-aware, (6) reject totals-only reports, (7) string-aware brace-matchers required, (8) two independent scans must converge.
evidence_refs: REVISION_HISTORY.md S802 entry (lines 16647–16668, 8 Permanent Prevention Rules)
REVISION_HISTORY.md lines 16145 (S801 false alarm root cause)

failures.name: Hash Drift & Governance Alarm Fatigue
failures.severity: Medium — false alarms consumed agent resources. Hash drift from authorized metadata changes (CognitiveLevel/DifficultyScore field additions) triggered hash-mismatch alerts across S719, S720, S722. May file hash drift observed in S707/S514 (not caused by session changes). scored_cases.js hash drift in S307, S501, S537 from line-ending conversion.
failures.what_happened: S63 baselines captured pre-700 pack file hashes. All 700-series sessions modified only CognitiveLevel and DifficultyScore fields (metadata-only). These legitimate changes triggered hash-mismatch blockers at session startup. Governance gates confused authorized metadata drift with unauthorized content contamination. May files (may-core.js, may-learner-state.js) showed hash drift from external modifications. scored_cases.js showed hash drift from line-ending conversion — binary content was identical.
failures.root_cause: Hash-based integrity checks treat all changes as equivalent — no distinction between authorized metadata edits and unauthorized content changes. Pre-700 baselines became stale as the 700-series program executed its design (metadata-only field additions). May files were modified outside the session governance framework.
failures.lesson: Hash checks must distinguish authorized metadata-only drift from unauthorized content drift. T0 baselines must be refreshed at the start of each governance program, not carried forward from pre-program snapshots. May files should be explicitly excluded from pack-level hash verification.
failures.prevention: CURRENT_BASELINES.md updated at S530 T0 snapshot capturing post-700 state. 700-series pre-flight protocol now verifies hashes against CURRENT_BASELINES.md (not S63). Pack file hash drift is pre-authorized for metadata-only sessions. Content/answer-key/scoring drift is separately verified via grep on CorrectChoice values, grep on question_state, and app.js hash (5A4338C6... stable across all 700-series).

successes.name: Boundary-Aware Object Parsing (Function Constructor)

CorrectChoice extracted from the same enclosing JSON object as ExplanationWrong fields — eliminating the forward-scan CC-offset that caused DL-029 false positives. String-aware brace-matcher replaced naive counter. QuestionID-to-next-QuestionID boundary windowing replaced fixed-window regex.
successes.impact: 100% accurate QID extraction. Zero DL-029 artifacts. All 2,500 items parseable across all 5 packs. methodology_improvements.name: T0 → Tmid → Tend Checkpoint Sequence
methodology_improvements.before: Sessions verified state at start only. No mid-session drift detection. No post-flight reconciliation. Hash mismatches caught only at session close.
methodology_improvements.after: Three-stage checkpoint: T0 (session start — all 13 runtime hashes verified), Tmid (~30 min or after 2+ agents — Pack D CAPA checks, app.js hash), Tend (session close — all 13 hashes vs T0, G1–G5 reconciliation if drift detected).
methodology_improvements.reliability_gain: Drift detected immediately at Tmid rather than at session close. Enabled concurrent-lane protection: S707 May file drift detected mid-session, attributed to external modification, not session-caused.

methodology_improvements.name: Backup-Before-Write Protocol
methodology_improvements.before: Some sessions wrote to pack files without backups. Concurrent-write data loss (DL-019) was the direct consequence — 432 overwritten items could not be restored from pre-write snapshot.
methodology_improvements.after: AGENTS.md §3: Hard rule. Before any edit/write against any pack file, copy to timestamped backup, confirm exists and non-zero, then proceed. Scored case files also covered.
methodology_improvements.reliability_gain: Zero unrecoverable writes since protocol adoption. S722A created 8 backups. S537 created 1 backup. All verified non-zero. Every 700-series write operation has a rollback path.
evidence_refs: DEFECT_LIBRARY.md DL-019 entry (lesson: every write must be preceded by backup)

methodology_improvements.name: Object-Bounded Verification (Within-Object CC Extraction)
methodology_improvements.before: Regex block-window scanning: extract QuestionID, search forward for CorrectChoice, evaluate EW[CC]. Produced ~75% false-positive rate because CC appears before QID in all 5 pack files (DL-029). Relied on brace-counter without string-awareness (DL-020).
methodology_improvements.after: Function constructor parse extracts complete question object. CorrectChoice read from the same enclosing JSON object as ExplanationWrong fields. Within-object methodology eliminates all cross-object contamination. G-NEW-3 enforcement: any scan tool must extract CC from the same enclosing object as the EW fields being evaluated.
methodology_improvements.reliability_gain: 100% accurate DL-008 detection. Zero cross-object false positives. Enabled S802 refutation of 67 Certified DL-008 claims. Enabled S701 verification that Pack D DL-008 was 20 (not 342).
evidence_refs: DEFECT_LIBRARY.md DL-029 entry (8 Permanent Prevention Rules)

methodology_improvements.name: Cross-Verification of Self-Reported Claims (AGENTS.md §5)
methodology_improvements.before: Agent self-reports accepted at face value. '0 remaining DL-008' claimed by 6-agent orchestration — but 175 items escaped in Pack C (DL-019). '197 cleared Pack C' claimed but 336 remained (DL-020 undercount). '75/63/47 DL-026' — three different counts from same broken tool accepted. '67 Certified DL-008' — DL-029 artifact accepted as P0 blocker.
methodology_improvements.after: AGENTS.md §5: Never accept summary reports at face value. Every self-reported claim must be cross-checked against raw file/line evidence. Specific cross-checks defined for certification complete, DL-008 violations, X items processed, validator pass, and zero errors. Totals-only reports without QID lists rejected. Two independent scans must converge before any remediation.
methodology_improvements.reliability_gain: S802 governance correction caught all 3 P0 S800 blockers as DL-029 artifacts by verifying against raw file evidence. Post-S722A verification: all 67 Certified DL-008 individually verified CLEAN via Function constructor parse. 2,181 Certified confirmed by 7 independent sources + raw grep — zero variance.
evidence_refs: AGENTS.md §5 (Dual Verification — Cross-Check All Self-Reported Claims)

methodology_improvements.name: CC-Position-Aware Scan Scripts (DL-029 Prevention Rule 3)
methodology_improvements.before: All scan scripts assumed CorrectChoice follows QuestionID in JSON object ordering. Zero scripts verified CC position in source file before running. Scripts were pack-agnostic — same tool used identically across all 5 packs despite different field orders.
methodology_improvements.after: Before any scan, verify CC position in source file for the specific pack being scanned. If CC precedes QID, forward-scan is forbidden. Function constructor parse is the universal fallback. S701 Pack D verification confirmed CC-before-QID positioning and switched to within-object extraction.
methodology_improvements.reliability_gain: Zero false positives from CC-offset in all post-S701 sessions. S802 confirmed CC-before-QID is universal across all 5 packs. 8 Permanent Prevention Rules codified.

methodology_improvements.name: Concurrent-Lane Protection Documentation
methodology_improvements.before: No tracking of which packs each session modified. Sessions operated in parallel on the same files with no coordination. DL-019 was the direct result.
methodology_improvements.after: Every session's REVISION_HISTORY.md entry explicitly lists Files Changed and Files NOT Changed. 700-series entries track which packs were modified by which agent and wave. S537 and S722A entries show all packs' protection status. This enables cross-session reconciliation and prevents concurrent writes by making modification scope transparent.
methodology_improvements.reliability_gain: Zero concurrent-write incidents in 700-series. Concurrent-lane protection verified at S722A post-flight: Pack B/C/D/E/app.js hashes all unchanged. May file hash drift attributed to external modification, not session-caused.

key_decisions.rationale: Prevents unauthorized writes in audit sessions. All exploratory and audit tasks operate read-only unless user explicitly authorizes writes with 'apply the fix,' 'make the change,' 'execute the write' or equivalent.
key_decisions.outcome: Successful — no audit-session write accidents across S718–S723 (read-only governance audits) and S800–S802 (governance correction lane). Enabled the 800-series correction lane that refuted 3 P0 blockers without modifying a single pack file.

key_decisions.rationale: Prevented bulk write accidents. Any change-set exceeding 30 question objects requires BLOCK-AUTHORIZED marker. This forces batch-level verification (backup, write, verify, confirm) rather than massive-blind-bulk operations.
key_decisions.outcome: Successful — S722A executed 83 items across 7 batches (all ≤28). S537 executed 49 state transitions in batches. DL-008 remediation executed in batches of ≤30 across all sessions. Zero batch-size violations. Enabled granular verification at batch boundaries.

key_decisions.rationale: Runtime delivery only pulls from strictly 'Certified' items. All other states (Unprocessed, In Audit, Editorial Queue, Archived) excluded. This gates learner safety on the HIGH-confidence AI verification + user approval certification process.

All DL-008/DL-013/DL-026 defects are in non-Certified items or remediated before certification. DL-030 answer-key errors (5 items) were all pre-700 and fixed before 700-series.

key_decisions.decision: AGENTS.md §12 — No Staged Findings (Log Before Session Close)
key_decisions.rationale: DL-019 (concurrent-write data loss) and DL-020 (validator brace-matcher undercount) were discovered but stored only in session reports — the defect library had no entries until a later session wrote them. The staged-findings pattern meant defects discovered in one session were invisible to the next.
key_decisions.outcome: Successful — Every session now produces minimum a REVISION_HISTORY.md entry as closing action. New defects logged to DEFECT_LIBRARY.md with next available DL-ID. Tracked notes enable cross-session tracking of partial states (e.g., 'Pack B Sections A/D certification-ready once metadata is fixed'). Zero 'lost discovery' incidents in 700-series.

recurring_root_causes: Template-based bulk authoring (5-item rotation groups) — produced DL-012 clones, DL-013 boilerplate, DL-015/016 metadata shifts, DL-025/026 empty distractor slots, DL-031 difficulty inflation, DL-032 uniform labeling. Single pipeline produced 10+ defect classes.

Scan methodology defects — without string-awareness, CC-position-awareness, or within-object verification, scans produced false positives (DL-029 ~75% FP rate), false negatives (DL-020 undercount), phantom counts (75/63/47 on clean file), and false TIER 1 classifications (AD-075).
Absence of coordination mechanisms — concurrent-write data loss (DL-019), no file-lock protocol, no session registry, no formal session-isolation enforcement.
Totals-only reporting — accepted without QID lists, making cross-verification impossible and enabling counting discrepancies to persist across sessions.
most_expensive_mistakes: DL-029 forward-scan false positives were the single most expensive error pattern — caused S800's 3 P0 blockers, triggered a near-miss massive false-alarm DL-008 remediation, consumed 26 agents across S800-S802 to refute, and delayed S803 by multiple sessions.
DL-019 concurrent-write data loss necessitated full re-remediation of 432 items (16 batches) that had already been correctly fixed.
Template-based bulk authoring created structural defects (DL-012, DL-013, DL-025, DL-026) whose remediation has consumed the largest share of agent-hours across all governance programs.
design_decisions_that_prevented_catastro: Read-only by default — prevented audit-session writes during the 800-series governance correction lane.
30-item batch cap — forced granular verification; a 500-item blind bulk write under DL-029 false positives would have corrupted hundreds of clean items.
Certified-only delivery pool — ensured that despite massive undercertification in Packs C/D and numerous open defects, zero defective items reached learners.
Governance guard automated enforcement — running continuously across all sessions rather than as a manual pre-release gate.
